newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ's Esanda half year net profit falls.
newsitem.headline: ANZ's Esanda half year net profit falls.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd's (ANZ) wholly-owned Esanda Finance Corp Ltd said on Tuesday net profit fell 20.4 percent to A$39 million for the six months to March 31 after restructuring costs of A$23.9 million.
Esanda said net profit before abnormals rose 28 percent to A$63 million.
Managing director Peter McMahon said the result was solid given the intensively competitive conditions in the finance industry.
Esanda provides asset-backed finance for vehicles, plant and equipment, property development, insurance premiums and fixed term investments and said it is Australia's largest finance company.
"Our underlying performance has improved due to growth in lending assets over the period and lower funding costs," McMahon said in a statement.
Total assets grew by 2.8 percent to A$9.3 billion.
Growth had been affected by subdued demand in new vehicle sales, with a corresponding impact on motor vehicle finance, and increasing competition in the motor vehicle finance sector.
McMahon said the restructuring programme underway at Esanda would continue through the second half of the financial year.
ANZ reported a 18 percent rise in group net profit for the six months to March 31 to A$615 million.
